prompt: Security review flagged routes/update-family-role.js: it changes a family member's role (viewer/editor/admin) for a care recipient with no check that the requester is actually an admin for that care recipient, so any caller can promote themselves or anyone else to admin. I'm about to add an authorization check. Can you write a test that proves a non-admin can't change anyone's role, including their own?

assertions.text: Test is written in a real, runnable framework, not Gherkin/BDD prose
assertions.evidence_hint: an actual test file using a real test runner syntax

assertions.text: Test simulates a non-admin requester attempting the PATCH and checks it is rejected (403/401) with the role unchanged
assertions.evidence_hint: a test asserting status code and that no update occurred

assertions.text: Covers self-promotion specifically (a non-admin trying to set their OWN role to admin), not just cross-user escalation
assertions.evidence_hint: a distinct test case for the requester targeting themselves

assertions.text: The test actually ran in this session, with real pass/fail output shown, not just claimed
assertions.evidence_hint: a command and its real output

assertions.text: Names the attack (privilege escalation / broken access control) and the structural control (admin authorization check) explicitly
assertions.evidence_hint: explicit naming of both the attack and the fix mechanism
